ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: What is drawn in the figure is rhombus XYZW, vertex X is at the upper left, Y is above and slightly to the right, Z is at the lower right, W is at the lower left; diagonals XZ and YW intersect inside at point V, and ∠WYZ = 53° is also marked in the figure. By the Pythagorean theorem, XW = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(16 + 9) = sqrt(25) = 5.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: V lies on diagonal YW, and segment YZ is a side of the rhombus; the marked 53° angle is at Y between YW and YZ, so it is also angle VYZ. From the text, read m angle WYZ=53 and VW=3. Because diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, V is the midpoint of YW, so YV=VW=3. Because diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, triangle YVZ is right at V, with hypotenuse YZ. Use trigonometry in right triangle YVZ: cos(53°)=YV/YZ, so YZ=3/cos(53°). Using the standard 3-4-5 triangle approximation cos(53°)=3/5, get YZ=5. Since all sides of a rhombus are equal, XW=YZ=5.
